title.narrative: Agricultural Value Chain Competitiveness and Safety

description.narrative: The project will strengthen value chains of competitive agricultural products (CAPs) cassava, mangoes, cashew nuts, vegetables, and native chicken in the provinces of Kampong Cham, Kampong Thom, Oddar Meanchey, Preah Vihear, Siem Reap, and Tboung Khmum. The project will (i) facilitate access to credit for agro-enterprises and agricultural cooperatives; (ii) promote viable market links among agro-enterprises and agricultural cooperatives, and enhance food safety and quality; and (iii) improve farm-to-market connectivity. The project will benefit 230 agricultural cooperatives (about 27,000 households) and about 50 agribusinesses in the project areas, and the number of beneficiaries will be expanded through intermediary financing.

Output: Agricultural value chain connectivity enhanced Indicator: About 3,000 road safety training participants, of which at least 50% are female, reported increased knowledge on the subject (baseline: 0, 0%). Achievement: 4479 Progress/Status: Road safety training has been completed in all six target provinces—Preah Vihear, Kampong Cham, Kampong Thom, Tboung Khmum, Siem Reap, and Oddar Meanchey—with a total of 4,479 participants, including 2,276 women (51%).
Participants' knowledge on road safety improved significantly, with the average test scores increasing from 56% (pre-test) to 88% (post-test). Among women participants, knowledge levels increased from 55% to 89% after the training. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports

Output: Agricultural value chain connectivity enhanced Indicator: At least 130 km of farm-to-market roads improved and climate-proofed to enhance connectivity between farms and markets (2020 baseline: 0 km). (RFI B) Achievement: 115.5 Progress/Status: A total of 115.5 km of farm-to-market roads (FMRs) across six target provinces have been fully rehabilitated (100% completed).
An additional 30.9 km of FMRs have been endorsed by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), and the ADB has issued a no-objection letter (NOL) to proceed with the contractor mobilization and road rehabilitation works, scheduled to begin in Q4 2025. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports

Output: Agricultural value chain financing enhanced Indicator: At least $40 million in AVC loans and equity capital loans provided to eligible borrowers, of which at least 25% ($10.0 million) is provided to women-owned PAEs and female borrowers (female farmers) (2020 baseline: $0, 0%) Achievement: 13748738 Progress/Status: A total of loans amounting to $13,748,738.10 (or 34.37% of the $40 million target) has been disbursed to 660 sub-borrowers. Of this amount, Sathapana Bank disbursed loans to 549 sub-borrowers totaling $8,771,738.10, while ARDB disbursed loans to 111 sub-borrowers totaling $4,977,000. The non-performing loan (NPL) ratio stands at 1.1%.
Of the total disbursed amount, $7,184,798 (equivalent to 17.96% of $40 million, or 52.28% of total loans disbursed) was provided to women-owned participating agro-enterprises. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports

Output: Agricultural value chain financing enhanced Indicator: At least 40% of AVC loan recipients are micro, small and medium-sized PAEs (2020 baseline: 0) (RFI A) Achievement: 14 Progress/Status: A total of 89 sub-loans have been disbursed to participating agro-enterprises (PAEs). Among them, 88 sub-borrowers are micro, small, and medium PAEs, representing 13.3% of the 660 total sub-borrowers, and 98.9% of all PAE sub-borrowers. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports

Output: Agricultural value chain financing enhanced Indicator: At least 50 government and PFI staff, of which at least 25% are female, report increased knowledge on AVC financing and credit guarantee and green financing (2020 baseline: 0, 0%) Achievement: 433 Progress/Status: A total of 433 participants from government agencies and participating financial institutions (PFIs) have enhanced their knowledge of agricultural value chain (AVC) financing and credit guarantee mechanisms. Among them, 85 participants (or 19.6%) are women. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports

Output: Agricultural value chain linkage and safety strengthened Indicator: About 230 PACs established IBPs with PAEs, of which at least 20% of PACs established contract farming arrangements or other alternative arrangements such as seasonal sales agreement (2020 baseline: 0, 0%) Progress/Status: A total of 25 producer agricultural cooperatives (PACs) have signed 27 sales contracts with five companies. Eleven Inclusive business partnership (BP) forums were conducted to promote market linkages.
The detailed engineering designs (DEDs) and bills of quantities (BOQs) for small-scale infrastructure have been completed, and ADB has approved the commencement of the bidding process. The works have been divided into three lots, which are currently being advertised. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Agricultural value chain linkage and safety strengthened Indicator: At least 10 PAEs obtained food safety assurance certificates (2020 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: A total of 287 staff from participating agricultural cooperatives (PACs) and participating agricultural enterprises (PAEs) have been trained on agri-product safety control, including 116 women (or 40%).
DAI is currently collaborating with four companies interested in obtaining Good Hygiene Practice (GHP) certification. In addition, DAI has conducted a comprehensive assessment and monitoring of 50 PAEs selected for ACSEP support, following their participation in the food safety training course. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Agricultural value chain linkage and safety strengthened Indicator: At least 30% of cassava PACs adopted disease cleaned materials and at least 30% of mango and cashew PACs adopted improved crop production practices and techniques and at least 30% of poultry farms adopted improved breeds, including at least 30% overall participation of women farmers (2020 baseline: 0%, 0%, 0%) Progress/Status: A total of 10,000 disease-free cassava stems have been produced and transferred to DoIC-GDA for multiplication. As cassava demonstrations require 510,000 stems, DoIC will collaborate with commercial farmers to further multiply the disease-free planting materials.
In addition, 2,000 mango seedlings of Keo Reach and Keo Tep varieties have been released as new varieties. Varietal development, trials, and demonstrations for disease-resistant and climate-resilient chili and cherry tomato are ongoing.
GDAHP has developed four commercial chick breeders to supply cross-bred chicks to farmers. The procurement of 113 greenhouses is being advertised.
A total of 37 crop demonstrations—including 9 on off-season mango production and 28 on cashew—have been successfully conducted. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Agricultural value chain linkage and safety strengthened Indicator: At least 350 farmers (PAC members), of which at least 60% are women, obtained CamGAP certificates (2020 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: A total of 2,167 farmers have been trained on the CamGAP Standard and Participatory Guarantee System (PGS), of whom 1,083 (or 50%) are women. Following the training, 300 farmers applied for CamGAP certification.
The General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA) is scheduled to begin the certification process in Q3 and Q4 2025, with an estimated 150 farmers expected to receive CamGAP certificates by the end of 2025. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Agricultural value chain linkage and safety strengthened Indicator: Integrated ICT data platform with geo-tagged farm level information built (baseline in 2020: None) Progress/Status: The Digitalization Strategic Plan was approved by the Minister of MAFF on 26 July 2024. The Agricultural Information and Documentation Centre (AiDOC) has identified priority investment items, including end-user computing equipment, GIS consultancy services, and a data center (server room) consultant. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports Actual value:
Value addition of five competitive agricultural value chains in the project areas increased

Products of at least 40 vegetable and/or poultry PACs sold their products at modern retail markets Progress/Status: Not yet due. 164 PACs have been selected as direct beneficiaries, with many involved in vegetable and poultry production.
Inclusive Business Partnership (IBP) forums have been conducted to link PACs and PAEs, including those involved in native chicken and vegetable production.
Demonstration farms and small infrastructure (e.g., vegetable net houses and chicken shelters) are being prepared to support production and market readiness.
Training on CamGAP and food safety standards has been provided to farmers and agro-enterprises, which is a prerequisite for accessing modern retail markets.Linking small producers to modern retail outlets is also a considerable leap. It is suggested, even at this stage, that the potential to achieve outcomes will need careful monitoring. Data Source: d. Quarterly project progress reports with inputs from PAEs Actual value:

Volume of cassava starch production increased to at least 150,000 tons per annum Progress/Status: Not yet due. CARDI has initiated multi-site experiments in five provinces to identify mosaic virus-resistant cassava varieties, and has produced 2,000 disease-free stems via tissue culture, with plans to produce 8,000 more in 2025. Due to limited production capacity, commercial sources will be needed to meet the demand for demonstration farms, which require over 500,000 stems. Cassava demonstration farms are planned and will begin in 2026, as the planting season for 2025 has passed. Data Source: c. Quarterly project progress reports with inputs from PAEs Actual value:

Volume of processed cashew increased to at least 15,000 tons per annum Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: This target is not yet due.
Foundational activities are underway, including the establishment of inclusive business partnerships (IBPs) and contract farming arrangements between PACs and cashew processing companies.
Demonstration farms for cashew cultivation have been planned, with cashew demos scheduled to commence in Q3 2025. Data Source: a. Quarterly project progress reports with inputs from PAEs

Volume of processed mango increased to at least 20,000 tons per annum Progress/Status: This target is not yet due.
Demonstration farms for mango cultivation have been planned, and implementation is expected to begin in Q3 2025.
The Cambodia Agricultural Research and Development Institute (CARDI) has released two new mango varieties—Keo Tep and Keo Reach—for domestic consumption, but no farm-level trials have been conducted yet.
ACSEP will focus on promoting best cultivation practices for mango rather than introducing new genetic varieties Data Source: b. Quarterly project progress reports with inputs from PAEs Actual value:
